relationships.subject: Hypericum sampsonii
relationships.evidence_quote: H. sampsonii significantly down-regulated the expression of NLRP3, Caspase-1, pro IL-1β, and IL-1β.

relationships.subject: Hypericum sampsonii
relationships.evidence_quote: LPS successfully induced the cells to activate TLR4, NF‐κB (p65), and upregulate the expression of NLRP3, pro IL‐1β, which was significantly suppressed after H. sampsonii intervention.

relationships.subject: TLR4/NF-kB signaling
relationships.evidence_quote: Lps-induced activation of the TLR4/NF-κB pathway promotes the expression of NLRP3 and pro-IL-1β

key_findings: H. sampsonii improved skin status, pain and serum IL-1beta, IL-6, TNF-alpha in radiodermatitis mice.
It suppressed NLRP3, caspase-1 and IL-1beta, likely via TLR4/NF-kB signal 1 inhibition in macrophages.
